content:
According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the progress of ChatGPT adoption through Apple Intelligence, saying its performance is "far below expectations," a situation that emerged after its 2024 launch. Details are as follows.

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, which has been merged into SpaceXAI, will sue Apple and OpenAI over allegations of alleged collusion to exclude competitors in the AI industry. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agreement with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the case was formally filed, the scope of the lawsuit has in fact gone beyond the App Store ranking issues that Musk initially publicly complained about. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of attempting to suppress the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to build an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the companies involved先后 submitted arguments, allegations, and rebuttals to the court. Apple and OpenAI一再 argued that the agreement is not the exclusive partnership alleged in the lawsuit; court documents submitted during the same period also revealed new details about how the two sides' collaboration operates.

One of the details was disclosed in a document OpenAI submitted today. According to the Financial Times, OpenAI "expressed disappointment at the low interest from iPhone users in the 'Apple Intelligence' ChatGPT feature following the agreement reached in 2024."

The report states:

Court documents unsealed on Wednesday show that when the agreement was reached in 2024, OpenAI had originally expected the promotion and brand collaboration with Apple to produce a "halo effect," and had anticipated gaining more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, within a month of the ChatGPT integration feature's launch, its performance "appeared to have a slow start," and OpenAI immediately downwardly revised its weekly active user growth forecast. The documents point out that by summer 2025, "it had become clearly apparent that Apple's integration of ChatGPT performed significantly below expectations."

The report points out that several segments of dialogue in today's filing were redacted, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately hopes to let users choose among different AI models, and specifically mentioned that Google Gemini could potentially become one of the integration options in the future.

That particular collaboration ultimately did not materialize, but Apple later switched to using Google's Gemini model to power the new Siri AI; Xcode has also expanded support for Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI's coding agent tools.

Returning to today's documents, the Financial Times mentions that the documents also point out that the way Apple implemented ChatGPT may be one of the reasons for the low adoption rate, because the relevant integration feature is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities disclosure filings have undermined SpaceXAI's claim that its partnership with Apple harmed competition. In its filing, OpenAI stated that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are "completely contrary to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit."

Based on the above reasons, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in favor of OpenAI on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before trial. The case is currently scheduled for trial in January.

Readers can find the relevant report in the Financial Times, as well as the Reuters report.
